title: The High Trail
premise: Hazel Thornbury, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, is drowning in debt when her old rival Silas Vane hires her crew to run a forbidden route upriver before monsoon season — carrying the inheritance of the man who once betrayed both their families. The cargo turns out to be a living heir: a runaway girl named Wren whose claim threatens the syndicate that owns the river's trade. Hunted by Vane's true employers and battered by storms, Hazel must choose between paying her debts and protecting the found family aboard her boat. In the end, Hazel scuttles the payment, exposes Vane's treachery at the river council, and loses the Kestrel to the flood — but gains a crew, a daughter-figure, and a new boat built from the wreck.
about_author: Beatrix Nakamura is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on tropical rivers before writing full-time. She lives in a stilt house with her partner, two dogs, and an alarming collection of salvaged ship wheels.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Introduces the Kestrel, her ragtag crew, and the crushing debt on the boat. A humiliating run downriver shows her skill reading water and her desperation. Emotional beat: pride worn thin by poverty.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ink
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The bank gives her one week before repossession. Crew members Bram and Odile quietly consider leaving; Hazel pretends not to notice. Emotional beat: fear masked as command.

chapters.title: The Man at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Silas Vane appears — the rival who testified against Hazel's father years ago — offering triple rate for a run up the Serrano River before landfall. Hazel refuses; the sworn-off route haunts her. Emotional beat: old rage resurfacing.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Hazel's POV: her father's last voyage up the Serrano, his disgrace, and Vane's role in it. Ends with Hazel waking to find the crew has voted to take the job without her blessing. Emotional beat: betrayal by family of choice.

chapters.title: Cargo Unknown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Loading day: a single sealed crate and a nervous broker who pays half upfront. Bram notices armed men watching the dock. Emotional beat: unease beneath relief.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A day out, they discover a girl hiding among the crates — Wren, sixteen, sharp-tongued, clearly the real cargo. She begs them not to turn back. Emotional beat: reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: Vane's Terms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A rendezvous with Vane's launch reveals he knows about Wren and demands she be delivered 'intact' to a man called Corvus at High Landing. Hazel realizes she's a kidnapper for hire. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. First storm squalls; Wren proves useful reading charts and reveals fragments of her story — an estate, a dead grandfather, a will. The crew begins to soften. Emotional beat: cautious belonging.

chapters.title: Leak at the Seams
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Kestrel takes damage running rapids; the hull begins seeping. Repairs cost them time as the monsoon front builds behind them. Emotional beat: dread made physical.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At a river trading post they learn who Corvus is: the syndicate boss who owns every dock on the Serrano and who destroyed Hazel's father. Wren is his granddaughter — and his heir's rival. Emotional beat: the past and present colliding.

chapters.title: The Broker's Men
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Armed skiffs shadow them through the narrows; a night chase ends with the Kestrel grounding on a sandbar only Hazel can read. They escape but lose their fuel reserve. Emotional beat: Hazel's knowledge as salvation.

chapters.title: Wren's Story
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Around a rain-drummed fire, Wren tells all: her grandfather's will names her, not Corvus, inheritor of the river charters. Corvus wants her delivered so the will can 'disappear.' Emotional beat: grief turning into resolve.

chapters.title: A Vote Below Decks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew votes secretly: finish the delivery and take the money, or turn upriver to the will's witnesses first. It splits three-two. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: High Landing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach High Landing and see Corvus's compound — and the scale of his power. Vane waits on the dock, too smooth, too watchful. Hazel stalls the handoff. Emotional beat: walking into the trap with eyes open.

chapters.title: The Handoff That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the exchange, Corvus's men try to take Wren and seize the Kestrel as well. A violent escape; Odile is wounded covering the retreat. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood.

chapters.title: Downstream Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Fleeing downstream means running the gauntlet of Corvus's checkpoints; upstream lies the witness who can validate the will — Hazel's father's old friend, presumed dead. Emotional beat: choosing the harder hope.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Radio warnings: landfall in four days. The sky goes green-black. Odile's fever rises from her wound. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: The Medicine Run
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A desperate stop at a floating market for antibiotics ends with Bram trading his father's compass ring — and learning Corvus has put a price on all their heads. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: Dead Man Upstream
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They find the witness, Tomas Reyes, alive in a cliffside mission — bitter, half-blind, and unwilling to help a Thornbury. Hazel must confront what her father actually did up here. Emotional beat: shame and reckoning.

chapters.title: Her Father's Logbook
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Tomas produces her father's logbook: he refused to falsify charter papers for Corvus and was ruined for it. Hazel weeps for the first time in the book. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed — integrity, not disgrace.

chapters.title: Tomas Decides
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV (single guest chapter). The old witness weighs his fear against his guilt over staying silent for twenty years. He agrees to come — if they swear the will gets read publicly at the river council. Emotional beat: redemption accepted late.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Vane intercepts them alone and offers Hazel everything: debt cleared, a new boat, her father's name restored — if she hands over Wren and Tomas. He claims he was coerced back then too. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren overhears enough of the offer to fear betrayal, then watches Hazel throw Vane off the boarding ladder into the river. Their trust is sealed. Emotional beat: daughter-figure earned, not declared.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The monsoon hits early and hard. The Kestrel fights white water; the leak worsens; they shelter in a flooded side channel as trees come down the current. Emotional beat: nature indifferent to their cause.

chapters.title: Bail and Prayers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A night of bailing, singing, and near-capsize binds the crew into something unbreakable. Odile's fever breaks at dawn. Emotional beat: joy inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Kestrel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Running the last gorge, the Kestrel tears open on submerged debris. They beach her sinking hull in a cove; the boat that carried everything is lost. Hazel grieves her father twice over. Emotional beat: devastating loss.

chapters.title: On Foot to Council Rock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The five trek overland through drowned country toward the river council at Council Rock, where charters are contested each season. Corvus's men are converging by water. Emotional beat: determination with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A crossing becomes a fight; Tomas is captured. The others escape but must choose: rescue him or make the council deadline. Emotional beat: impossible arithmetic of loyalty.

chapters.title: Split Currents
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel sends Wren and Odile ahead to the council while she and Bram go back for Tomas. First time Hazel and Wren separate since the stowaway discovery. Emotional beat: trust tested at distance.

chapters.title: Corvus's Court
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reaches Council Rock to find Corvus already there, charming the council, with Tomas as his 'guest.' She must testify without her witness or her captain. Emotional beat: standing alone.

chapters.title: The Rescue at the Weir
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Bram free Tomas from a weir-side camp using rivercraft tricks against armed men — flooding a lock, cutting moorings. Vane, present, hesitates and lets them pass. Emotional beat: the rival's conscience stirring.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren speaks to the council: her grandfather's will, Corvus's falsified charters, the men he ruined — naming Hazel's father. The hall goes silent. Emotional beat: courage as inheritance.

chapters.title: Vane Turns
chapters.summary: Vane's POV (second guest chapter). Arriving soaked from the weir, Vane delivers the logbook and confesses his coercion and crimes, burning his own standing to end Corvus. Emotional beat: ruin chosen as penance.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The council validates the will, voids Corvus's charters, and orders his arrest. Corvus tries to flee by launch and is taken by the flooded river itself. Emotional beat: power drowning in its own element.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Aftermath at Council Rock: Wren offers Hazel a charter and partnership; Hazel asks instead for salvage rights to the Kestrel's hull. Emotional beat: humility after victory.

chapters.title: Salvage
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crew returns to the cove and raises what remains of the Kestrel. Her keel is sound. They begin rebuilding on the riverbank as a community gathers to help. Emotional beat: resurrection by many hands.

chapters.title: Debts Paid Forward
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hazel uses Wren's first charter payment to clear the bank debt — then signs the boat over to the crew collectively, herself included as equal share. Emotional beat: ownership redefined as belonging.

chapters.title: Naming Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The rebuilt boat is launched. Wren suggests the name; they keep Kestrel, repainted, scarred, stronger. Hazel scatters her father's logbook pages' ashes-free copy in the current. Emotional beat: grief finally given a ceremony.

chapters.title: First Charter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The new Kestrel's maiden run carries honest cargo and free passengers — including Tomas going home. Wren stands at the wheel Hazel taught her to read. Emotional beat: legacy passed forward.

chapters.title: Every Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Closing mirror of chapter one: same river, same sandbars, different woman at the helm — surrounded by crew, debt-free, at peace. Final line: the river keeps its moods, but no longer hers alone. Emotional beat: homecoming.
